title: Retirement residency in Malaysia for Singaporeans who want to age there
asked: Whether the Government will engage Malaysia to establish an affordable long-stay or retirement-residency pathway for Singaporeans who wish to age in Malaysia and access more affordable eldercare there, given that the revised Malaysia My Second Home scheme now targets investors rather than retirees.
response: Mr Tan Kiat How said every country sets its own residency requirements and policies for foreign nationals' access to social services, and some countries may offer a lifestyle service for foreigners to retire. He said Singapore's focus is on ensuring all Singaporeans have access to quality and affordable eldercare in Singapore now and into the future. In a supplementary answer, he said the Government recognises some Singaporeans may choose to live, retire or take private healthcare elsewhere, respects those choices and respects Malaysia's sovereignty over its policies. He said the priority is supporting Singaporeans who want to age in place in the community, through an eldercare ecosystem, care standards, recourse, Active Ageing Centres and the Age Well SG and Age Well Neighbourhoods programmes.

key_points.point: Each country determines its own residency requirements and policies for foreign nationals' access to social services.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: every country will determine its residency requirements and policies for foreign nationals' access to their social services.

key_points.point: Some countries may offer a lifestyle service for foreigners to retire in their countries.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: Some countries may offer a lifestyle service for foreigners to retire in their countries.

key_points.point: Singapore's focus is on ensuring all Singaporeans have access to quality and affordable eldercare in Singapore as they age.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: Our focus is on ensuring that all Singaporeans have access to quality and affordable eldercare in Singapore as they age, now and into the future.

key_points.point: The Government recognises that some Singaporeans may choose to live, retire or take private healthcare elsewhere for their own reasons.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: we recognise that some Singaporeans may choose to live, retire or take private healthcare elsewhere for their own reasons.

key_points.point: The Government respects every sovereign nation, including Malaysia, on policies for foreign nationals' access to social services, care, or residency status.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: We also respect every other sovereign nation, including Malaysia, on the policies they make with respect to allowing for foreign nationals to access their social services, care, or for their residency status.

key_points.point: Many seniors, families and caregivers want to age in place in the community, near family and friends in familiar neighbourhoods.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: we have come across many seniors, many families and caregivers who want to age in place in the community, age in place near their family, near their friends, in the neighbourhoods which they are familiar with.

key_points.point: There is an eldercare ecosystem, a good standard of care, and recourse for individuals if the quality of care falls short.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: making sure that there is an eldercare ecosystem, making sure that there is a good standard of care, making sure that there is recourse for individuals if the quality of care falls short.

key_points.point: The Government has the Age Well SG programme and the Age Well Neighbourhoods programme.
key_points.speaker: Mr Tan Kiat How
key_points.quote: That is why we have the Age Well SG programme, we have the Age Well Neighbourhoods programme.

left_open: Whether the Government will engage Malaysia on an affordable long-stay or retirement-residency pathway for Singaporeans.
Whether the Government will negotiate with Malaysian federal and state authorities to expand Sarawak's no-investment-needed residency scheme to West Malaysia.
